newsitem.title: FRANCE: Zeroual ally forms Algerian political party.
newsitem.headline: Zeroual ally forms Algerian political party.

text.p: A close ally of Algerian President Liamine Zeroual announced on Friday the creation of a political party, ahead of elections this year seen by the authorities as a way of ending violence in which about 60,000 people have died.

Abdelkader Bensalah, president of Algeria's unelected stand-in parliament, said the party, the National Democratic Rally (Rassemblement National Democratique), was a message of hope and peace and would be open to all.
Its formation follows the murder last month of Algeria's powerful trade union boss Abdelhak Benhamouda who had planned to step down from his post and form a party expected also to back Zeroual.
The authorities blamed Moslem fundamentalists for Benhamouda's killing in central Algiers.
Bensalah told reporters, in a statement carried by the official news agency APS, that the new party "claimed no monopoly, would have no exclusion..."
"Essentially democratic, the RND has faith in pluralism and alternance of power and the virtues of liberty," he said.

It would work to "encourage freedom of expression, anchor the principle of social justice, human rights and national solidarity, while working in favour of Algeria's development and progress in a climate of security, stability and concord."

Zeroual has promised that a general election will be held in the first half of this year, followed by local elections. The Algerian authorities have excluded any participation by the outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) which held a massive lead in a general election cancelled in January 1992.
Violence erupted shortly afterwards and has constantly escalated.
Bensalah, born in 1941, was a member of parliament from 1977 to 1989 when he was appointed ambassador to Saudi Arabia, a post he held until 1992.
He became foreign ministry spokesman before being elected in May 1994 to head the unelected Transitional National Council which acted as a quasi-parliament to pass government laws.
